common_name: Constance Spry Rose (First David Austin English Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation and support for training, since Constance Spry is a large, vigorous, once-blooming shrub best grown as a short climber against a wall, fence, or pillar.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, providing a trellis, pillar, or fence if training the long canes upward. Introduced by David Austin in 1961, Constance Spry was the first rose in what became the English Rose line, bearing huge, cupped, clear pink peony-like blooms carrying a rich, unusual myrrh fragrance that David Austin had not previously found in a modern rose. Unlike most later English roses it blooms only once, in a spectacular, heavy flush in late spring, on a large, vigorous, thorny shrub or short climber, so it is best sited where its single dramatic display and handsome foliage justify the space; some gardeners underplant it with later-blooming perennials to extend seasonal interest.

common_name: Heritage Rose (Classic David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Heritage is an older David Austin introduction and can be somewhat more susceptible to black spot than newer, disease-bred cultivars, so good air movement and routine care matter.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, and prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood. Introduced by David Austin in 1984, Heritage is one of the most beloved and enduring early English roses, carrying soft shell-pink, cupped, shallowly rosetted blooms with a distinctive lemony myrrh fragrance that helped define the fragrance profile many gardeners now associate with English roses. Its graceful, arching, densely foliaged shrub and reliably repeat-blooming habit from late spring through frost have kept it in continuous cultivation for decades, and it remains a benchmark for softness of color and fragrance among pink English roses.

common_name: Benjamin Britten Rose (David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Benjamin Britten's compact, bushy habit and strong disease resistance make it a good choice for a smaller mixed border.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, and prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood. Introduced by David Austin in 2001 and named for the English composer, Benjamin Britten bears vivid orange-red to crimson, cupped rosette blooms with a strong, fruity fragrance carrying notes of blackcurrant, on a compact, bushy, disease-resistant shrub. Its vivid, saturated warm color reads strongly even at a distance in the border, and it repeat-blooms freely from late spring through frost with routine feeding and deadheading, holding clean foliage well through humid summers.

common_name: Malvern Hills Rose (David Austin English Rambling Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun to partial shade with sturdy support, since Malvern Hills is an extremely vigorous rambler best trained over a large arch, pergola, or fence where its long canes have room to spread.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in fertile, well-drained soil, training the long, flexible canes over sturdy support such as an arch, pergola, or large fence, since Malvern Hills is one of the more vigorous, rambling David Austin introductions rather than a compact border shrub. Small, soft yellow, rosette-shaped flowers open in dense clusters in a single heavy flush in late spring, carrying a light, fresh fragrance, and the shrub's shade tolerance and vigor make it useful for covering a difficult structure or fence line that would defeat a less rambunctious climber. Prune immediately after the spring bloom to shape and remove old wood, since it flowers primarily on growth made the previous year.

common_name: Grace Rose (David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Grace's slightly nodding flower habit shows the blooms to good effect on a raised bed or slope where they can be viewed from below.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, and prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood. Introduced by David Austin in 2001, Grace bears warm apricot, deeply cupped rosette blooms with a light tea fragrance, on a vigorous, well-branched shrub whose slightly nodding flower habit distinguishes it from more upright-facing English rose cultivars. Its warm, glowing apricot tone pairs well with both cool blues and other warm-toned companions in a mixed border, and it repeat-blooms reliably from late spring through frost with routine feeding and deadheading.
